## Learning Outcomes

::: {.section-intro}
By the end of this course, students should be able to:
:::

::: {.outcomes-grid}

::: {.outcome-item}
::: {.outcome-num}
1
:::
To empower higher education faculty in Kenya with the knowledge, tools, and strategies to effectively integrate sustainable development (SD) concepts and theories into their teaching.
:::

::: {.outcome-item}
::: {.outcome-num}
2
:::
To provide an in-depth understanding of key SD concepts and theories.
:::

::: {.outcome-item}
::: {.outcome-num}
3
:::
To guide participants in establishing thematic connections between SD and their respective fields.
:::

::: {.outcome-item}
::: {.outcome-num}
4
:::
To highlight the importance of Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) for sustainable futures, and to provide knowledge, tools, and strategies to integrate ESD approaches into their teaching.
:::

::: {.outcome-item}
::: {.outcome-num}
5
:::
To develop an individual action plan on how to integrate SD and ESD approaches into teaching.
:::

::: {.outcome-item}
::: {.outcome-num}
6
:::
Communicate sustainability challenges to diverse audiences including policy makers and civil society.
:::

:::

:::

## Course Sessions

::: {.section-intro}
The course runs over 5-6 weeks combining lectures, workshops, field sessions, and guest expert inputs.
Each session page includes materials, tasks, and localisation notes for partner institutions.
:::

::: {.cde-cards}

::: {.cde-card .cde-card-individual}
::: {.cde-card-accent}
:::
::: {.cde-card-body}
[Foundations]{.cde-card-tag}
### Session 01: Introduction to Sustainable Development

Participants learn to define sustainable development and its core principles, identify key challenges that sustainability seeks to address.
:::
::: {.cde-card-footer}
[View session](sessions/week-01.qmd){.cde-card-link}
:::
:::

::: {.cde-card .cde-card-individual}
::: {.cde-card-accent}
:::
::: {.cde-card-body}
[Foundations]{.cde-card-tag}
### Session 02: Interlinkages of Sustainability Dimensions and Role of Science & Education

Participants examine the links between social, economic, and environmental dimensions of sustainable development. 
:::
::: {.cde-card-footer}
[View session](sessions/week-02.qmd){.cde-card-link}
:::
:::

::: {.cde-card .cde-card-individual}
::: {.cde-card-accent}
:::
::: {.cde-card-body}
[Foundations]{.cde-card-tag}
### Session 03: Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) & Constructive Alignment

Participants gain an understanding of the principles and importance of ESD as well as of the concept of constructive alignment in designing effective courses.
:::
::: {.cde-card-footer}
[View session](sessions/week-03.qmd){.cde-card-link}
:::
:::

::: {.cde-card .cde-card-individual}
::: {.cde-card-accent}
:::
::: {.cde-card-body}
[Presentations]{.cde-card-tag}
### Session 04: Presentation of Action Plans

Participants present the action plan they have developed on how to integrate (E)SD into their own teaching. .
:::
::: {.cde-card-footer}
[View session](sessions/week-04.qmd){.cde-card-link}
:::
:::

::: {.cde-card .cde-card-individual}
::: {.cde-card-accent}
:::
::: {.cde-card-body}
[Reflexions]{.cde-card-tag}
### Session 05: Reflection session

Participants provide feedback on course content, structure, etc.
:::
::: {.cde-card-footer}
[View session](sessions/week-05.qmd){.cde-card-link}

## Adapt This Course

This course is designed to be adopted and adapted by Higher Education Institutions worldwide.
Materials are modular — individual sessions can be integrated without running the full course.
Each session includes a **recommendations for facilitation**.
